newsitem.title: GERMANY: Mannesmann 1996 net falls to 600 mln DM.
newsitem.headline: Mannesmann 1996 net falls to 600 mln DM.

text.p: German engineering and telecommunications group Mannesmann AG said its group net profit fell to about 600 million marks ($354 million) in 1996 from 701 million the year before.
Group income from ordinary activities rose about 10 percent to about one billion marks. Management proposed a dividend of nine marks, up from eight marks.

The company said its automotive and especially its telecommunications divisions improved earnings last year while its engineering division earned only a "very small profit" due to a heavy loss at its Demag subsidiary.
The tubes and trading division made a loss, and tax payments increased in 1996.
Group sales rose eight percent to 34.7 billion marks, but adjusted for changes to the consolidated group they grew 10 percent, Mannesmann said.
Domestic sales were 15 billion marks, up from 14 billion marks, while international sales were 19.7 billion marks, up from 18 billion marks.
Incoming orders rose two percent, or four percent if adjusted for consolidation. The workforce declined to 119,675 from 122,684.
The data were preliminary and were to be presented by the management board at a meeting of the supervisory board later on Thursday, Mannesmann said.
Mannesmann said profit in its telecommunications businesses more than doubled in 1996, even after start-up losses for new activities.

In 1995, the telecommunication division profits totalled 464 million marks. The company gave no figure for 1996. The company said turnover in telecoms rose 55 percent to 4.2 billion marks, accounting for 12 percent of group turnover.
